Judgment

This first appeal has been preferred by the appellants/landowners challenging the order dtd.07.04.1999 passed by 6th Additional District Judge, Jabalpur in Land Acquisition case No.13/1992 affirming the award dtd. 06.02.1991 passed by Land Acquisition Officer.
2.

Short facts of the case are that, land having an area 0.482 hectare of Khasra No.100/4 situated in Tahsil Kundam, District Jabalpur was acquired in the year 1988-89 regarding which an award of Rs.17,739/- was passed by Land Acquisition Officer on 06.02.1991.
Upon filing application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (in short 'the Act') by the land owners, matter was referred to the Court.

In support of the claim submitted by the appellants of an amount of Rs.6,75,000/-, they adduced evidence and examined Uttam Kumar Rai (AW-1), Sushil Kumar Rai (AW-2) and Shyam Bihari Khare (AW-3) and also produced certified copies of the sale deeds (Ex.P/1 to P/5).
Respondents also examined witnesses Devendra Singh Kaurav (NAW-1) and Kamal Singh Dhurve (NAW-2) and produced documentary evidence also.

While passing the impugned order, Additional District Judge did not consider the sale deeds (Ex.P/1 to P/5) produced by the appellants for want of examination of the witnesses as well as vendor and vendee of the sale deeds and taking into consideration the other material including the oral evidence available on record dismissed the claim and affirmed the award passed by Land Acquisition Officer.
Against which instant first appeal has been filed claiming compensation amount of Rs.2,24,000/- and an amount of Rs.15,260/- has been paid as court fees.

4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that as per section 51-A of the Act, certified copies of Smt.Baini Bai & Ors. vs The State Of M.P. & Anr. on 10 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21403441/

sentences.text: sale deeds can be accepted as evidence even without formal proof thereof by examination of the witnesses or by vendor and vendee of the sale deeds and court below has committed illegality in discarding the sale deeds of the favour of appellants for want of examination of witnesses as well as the vendor and vendee of the sale deeds (Ex. P/1 to P/5).

He submits that as the court below has not taken into consideration the sale deeds of the favour of appellants, therefore, has committed material illegality in passing the impugned order and prays for remand of the case for consideration afresh after taking into consideration the sale deeds (Ex.P/1 to P/5).
5 .
Learned counsel appearing for respondent/State supports the impugned award and prays for dismissal of the first appeal.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.
Land Acquisition Officer awarded an amount of Rs.17,739/- towards acquisition of land area 0.482 hectare of khasra No.100/4 owned by the appellants.

Apparently, by the impugned order,
reference Court has affirmed the award passed by Land Acquisition Officer after discarding certified copies of sale deeds (Ex.P/1 to P/5).
As such reference court has not considered any 3 FA-426-1999 documentary evidence produced by the appellants in support of their claim of Rs.6,75,000/-.

8. Section 51-A of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 provides as under :
"51-A. Acceptance of certified copy as evidence.

In any proceeding under this Act, a certified copy of a document registered under the Registration Act, 1908 (16 of 1908),
including a copy given under section 57 of that Act, may be accepted as evidence of the transaction recorded in such documents."

9 . Apparently the court below has not taken into consideration the aforesaid provision contained in Section 51-A of the Act and has discarded certified copies of registered sale deeds (Ex. P/1 to P/5) for want of examination of witnesses and vendor and vendee of the sale deeds.
10.

In my considered opinion the reference court has committed grave illegality in discarding certified copy of registered sale deeds (Ex.P/1 to P/5) for want of examination of witnesses and vendor and vendee of the sale deeds and non-consideration of the same has caused serious injustice to the appellants.
11.

Resultantly, the matter deserves to be and is hereby remanded to the court below (i.e. 6th Additional District Judge, Jabalpur) for decision of the Land Acquisition Case No.13/1992 afresh after taking into consideration certified copies of the registered sale deeds (Ex.P/1 to P/5) along with other evidence, with the further direction to restore the land acquisition case No.13/1992 to its original number.
12. Parties are directed to appear before the court below on 12.08.2024.
1 3 . Registry is directed to send back the record to the court below before 12.08.2024.
